note: All listed programs are online, GRE not required (optional at most). Fit assumes Boston College physics undergrad + ~4 years Capital One SWE. UChicago MPCS (true CS master's) is campus-only, so it is not listed.

schools.why: Built for people who did not major in CS. Physics counts as the quantitative proof they want. Your SWE job is extra, not required.
schools.fitNote: Easiest Ivy admit on this list — but the coursework starts at CS foundations. May feel basic after 4 years at Capital One.
schools.notes: Spring 2027: opens May 22, 2026; final deadline Oct 26, 2026.

schools.why: Official path for physics majors with 2+ years as a software engineer. Better academic match than MAS-CS given your job.
schools.fitNote: This is the Penn program I would actually apply to. MSE-AI is a worse bet — they want a CS/CE undergrad degree, which you don't have.
schools.notes: Same cycle as MAS-CS. Need 2 recommenders + personal statement.

schools.why: No GRE. Physics + SWE is a normal profile here. Live evening classes work if you stay in Chicago.
schools.fitNote: This is UChicago's actual online master's — MPCS (CS) is in-person only. Diploma is Applied Data Science, not Computer Science.
schools.notes: Autumn 2027 online deadline June 23, 2027. Portal can close early if the cohort fills.

schools.why: Non-CS undergrads can apply if they have OOP, data structures, algorithms — your Capital One work covers that.
schools.fitNote: Real CS master's, well-known, designed for working engineers. Strong middle of this list.
schools.notes: Letters of rec not required. Recommended GPA 3.2+.

schools.why: They want a science/engineering bachelor's + real programming. Physics + Java/backend work matches.
schools.fitNote: US News has ranked this online IT/CS program very highly. Rolling-ish decisions, 3 starts a year.
schools.notes: Spring 2027 deadline Nov 1, 2026. Need 3 letters of recommendation.

schools.why: Built for working engineers/scientists. Physics undergrad + SWE is a standard admit profile. Rolling, ~2–3 week decisions.
schools.fitNote: High chance, real CS master's, less 'brand heat' than Penn/UChicago/GT for some employers — still a strong name.
schools.notes: 3 starts (fall/spring/summer). Missing undergrad CS prereqs can be filled after a provisional admit.

schools.why: Physics is STEM (preferred). No GRE. Best cost/reputation on the list. They officially say work experience rarely replaces CS coursework.
schools.fitNote: You can get in, not a lock. Spell out data structures/algorithms from Capital One in the application. Hardest coursework of this list.
schools.notes: Need 3 recommenders. Admitted students start conditionally (must pass 2 foundation courses with B or better).

schools.why: They want discrete math, data structures, algorithms, computer systems. Your job helps; missing undergrad CS theory is the risk.
schools.fitNote: Reach-er than UIUC/Rice for a physics major. Still worth a shot if you want a CS (not DS) degree from a big name.
schools.notes: No one is auto-admitted. GRE optional if you want extra proof of quant.
